children: Immutep reported statistically significant, exposure-dependent immune suppression after a single IMP761 infusion in a Phase I study of 60 healthy volunteers. The drug was well tolerated across seven dose levels; no serious or severe adverse events were reported.
Significant, exposure-dependent suppression after one infusion
Clinical proof-of-concept supports IMP761's potential in autoimmune disease; no prior-period comparison was provided.
Well tolerated across 0.03–14 mg/kg dose levels
The release reports no serious or severe adverse events, supporting continued dose escalation.
MAD results anticipated in H1 CY2027
The ongoing analysis is expected to inform dose selection for a potential Phase II program.
Preclinical RA samples showed reduced T-cell activation
These findings add supporting evidence for the autoimmune rationale but are preclinical.

This is an early clinical proof-of-concept update, building on positive first-in-human results presented at EULAR 2026. The next catalyst is the anticipated H1 CY2027 report from the multiple ascending dose portion, which is expected to inform potential Phase II dose selection.
